The four longevity pieces: ORAC is one quarter of Wallach's anti-aging answer, and minerals are a separate piece
  ↳ Luneth's critique of the ORAC demo asked a question the page could not answer: if antioxidants only raise the AVERAGE lifespan and not the maximum, what raises the ceiling? Pages 376-377 carry the same two-column OCR fusion as the earlier chunks - 'There is an accumulated knowledge, however, thatyeyeals the simple and universal common threads' is the left column's '...however, that' welded onto the right column's 'reveals the simple...'. Getting the reading order right mattered and was easy to get wrong, so both columns of the page image were read separately at 2.7x: page 376 ends mid-sentence on '...beyond 100 years is' and page 377 picks it up with 'that: 1) consciously or unconsciously...'. A second fix repaired lost word spacing on the Land Mines opening, which would otherwise have shipped as 'thatwillcertainly preventyoufrom' inside a quote users actually read. Nine claims landed, every verbatim snapped to exact book bytes: the four pieces; that every human has the genetic equipment to live well beyond 100; 'beautiful, healthful and functional' - which is Wallach's own answer to the objection that a longer life just means a longer old age; the genetics rebuttal that even if everyone in your family died at 35 you can still reach 100; the 20 to 25 years the industrialized world is losing, with America sliding from 17th to 48th; calorie restriction at 1,250-1,800; the line that a high-protein low-carb diet is forgiving of low vitamins but unforgiving of low minerals; where Blue Zone populations actually got their minerals; and the land mines themselves. And corpus_seal refused outright with 'claim references unknown/unhashed book' because the spacing fix was applied after the last resnap, leaving the book hash stale - the exact ordering trap the resnap documentation warns about. ## 2026-07-23 20:07 UTC-05:00 · build · knowledge
Drawer menu to 0.65rem and optically centered - it was already geometrically centered, which is why it looked wrong
  ↳ The knowledge drawer's tab menu is now 0.65rem and sits centered between the KNOWLEDGE mark and the close button. THE INTERESTING PART. The menu was ALREADY dead-center in the header - measured offset 0px from the content box midpoint. Had I trusted that number and replied 'it is centered', I would have been correct and useless. What made it read as left-shifted is that the two side columns were each flex: 1 1 0, so each claimed an equal 101px, but their VISIBLE content differs completely: the left column is filled by the 'KNOWLEDGE' text, while the right holds a 34px close button flush right with roughly 67px of empty column beside it. The eye therefore measured 24px of gap after the mark and about 91px before the [X]. Geometric centering and optical centering were not the same thing, and the eye was right. THE FIX. Both side columns size to their content (flex: 0 0 auto) and the tab pill takes margin-inline: auto, so the leftover space splits evenly around the thing you can actually see. Measured after: 77px of gap on each side, tabs center 723 exactly equal to the midpoint between the mark's right edge and the button's left edge. THE FONT. 0.65rem is a literal, not a token: it sits between --ds-text-micro (0.6rem) and --ds-text-mini (0.7rem), so no token expresses it and borrowing the nearest one would have said something false about the value. VERIFICATIONS: invariants 77/77, render_probe_knowledge and render_probe_search exit 0. The probe asserts the two GAPS are equal, deliberately, rather than asserting the pill is centered in its container - the container-centering property was already TRUE while the defect stood, so testing it would have passed and proved nothing. Picking the assertion that can actually fail is the whole job.

## 2026-07-23 19:41 UTC-05:00 · build · knowledge
Best-match block pins exact title hits on every filterable tab; Explore gets a search bar that searches content
  ↳ Typing 'acne' on the Conditions tab used to match every condition whose CLAIMS mention acne, ordered by claim count, so the actual Acne page sat far down a list of 31 results. Real title matches are now pinned in a 'Best match' strip at the top, most-exact always first. The Explore tab, which had no filter at all, now has one - and it searches content, not just chip labels. RANKING (Luneth's spec). AND-over-terms on the TITLE, which is what makes a multi-word query narrow rather than widen: 'cancer' pins Cancer plus 11 more cancers, while 'breast cancer' pins only Breast Cancer, because no other title carries both terms. Rank 0 = the title IS the query, and that slot is reserved so a perfect match can never be outranked; 1 = starts-with; 2 = merely contains; ties break on the shorter title so 'Cancer' precedes 'Cancer, Breast'. Cap 12: one exact plus up to eleven. WHY TITLES NEEDED THEIR OWN SOURCE. The data-search blob deliberately makes a row match on content - that is the feature that lets 'smell' find Anosmia - but it is also exactly what buries a title hit. So ranking reads the title alone, via a per-tab KD_TITLE_SELECTOR, while filtering keeps using the blob. HOISTED, NOT CLONED. The pinned rows are the ORIGINAL DOM nodes, moved. They therefore keep their per-tab styling and their delegated click handlers, and they cannot render twice - Luneth chose 'disappear from the bottom results' explicitly. Each move records where it came from, and every keystroke restores the previous set before ranking again, so ordering never compounds on itself. applyKnowledgeSearch was restructured into restore -> mark -> hoist -> head-pass, in that order, so a section whose rows were ALL hoisted reports itself empty instead of showing a head over nothing. EXPLORE CONTENT SEARCH. Each chip now carries a data-search blob of the entity's lay synonyms, its claims' topic tags, and its claims' QUESTION text - questions are phrased the way people actually search. Answer and verbatim bodies are deliberately excluded: they would multiply the attribute across every chip and make a topic match on one incidental word, which reads as a false positive. VERIFICATIONS: build OK, invariants 77/77, four render probes exit 0. Browser-verified: 'acne' pins Acne first (previously buried among 31 results), 'cancer' pins Cancer then eleven more cancers, 'breast cancer' pins exactly one, clearing the query restores all 502 rows with zero hidden and removes the block, the Explore bar exists, 'celiac' matches three Explore chips through their claim questions, and Explore 'mercury' pins Mercury first. INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first verification run reported nonsense - 'acne' pinned as '9'. That was the PROBE reading a condition row's big ghost claim-count as its title, not a fault in the feature. Fixed in the probe. Worth recording because a wrong instrument that returns plausible-looking output is the failure mode that wastes the most time.

It is now the same light cream as the demo, and the top bar is untouched exactly as he asked. The measurement changed the diagnosis, which is the part worth recording. I sampled real pixels from both pages rather than trusting my eye, and the tan box itself is rgb(235,226,196) in BOTH live and demo — the box was never the problem. The difference was the SURROUND: rgb(242,231,207) live against rgb(250,245,232) in the demo. And that exposed the actual defect, which is more interesting than "too dark": the surround (242,231,207) was DARKER than the box interior it contains (242,234,211). Inverted figure/ground — a raised plate sitting on a dimmer page. That is what reads as muddy. In the demo the box is darker than its surround, which is the way round a raised plate has to be. There were two causes: .app-workspace paints --ds-paper-deep, and .app-workspace::before is a viewport-fixed radial veil that tints whatever sits under it. The fix is deliberately NOT the demo's. The demo sets .app-workspace to --ds-paper and kills the veil outright. But that veil is position:fixed with inset:0, so it covers the TOPBAR too — it is exactly why live's topbar reads (249,244,231) where the demo's reads (250,245,232). Luneth kept the live topbar explicitly, so the veil had to survive. THE ONE LOAD-BEARING DECISION: regimen state lives in ONE atomic localStorage document (rgSlots_v1 = {slots[], activeSlot, trash[]}) written by ONE private function (writeSlotDoc). localStorage has no transaction across keys, so a single key is the only way a slot switch / delete / remove / restore can be all-or-nothing — a second key for the trash would put a torn-write data-loss window on the everyday remove path. Chosen after an 11-agent adversarial workflow (3 candidate designs × 3 judge lenses + synthesis): the one-key document won on engineering-doctrine (atomic ops, single source of truth) AND blueprint fidelity; the two-key and roster-only rivals were rejected (torn-write data-loss / unforced under-delivery of the signed-off §3 model). WHAT CHANGED. core/schemas/regimen.ts: NEW SlotSchema/TrashEntrySchema/SlotDocSchema (+ a bounded, control/bidi-safe SlotNameSchema); the Zod schema enforces >=1/<=4 slots, <=20 trash, and activeSlot-always-resolves at BOTH the read and write boundary, so a torn or hand-edited document cannot be read back as valid — a null read re-synthesises a clean Default (auto-heal). state/regimen.ts: the private writeSlotDoc is the sole setValidated(rgSlots_v1) writer + the emit; a lazy, non-destructive read-time migration rebuilds a Default slot from the four legacy keys (reproducing the old effective-stack math), recovers any hidden items INTO the trash, and leaves the legacy keys inert on disk (rollback safety); the five legacy chokepoints keep their exact names + signatures (so the burning views compile) but re-point into the active slot; saveRgRemoved/loadRgRemoved became trash adapters; NEW slot ops addSlot/duplicateSlot/deleteSlot/renameSlot/setActiveSlot/restoreFromTrash, each returning {ok}|{ok:false,reason} — a refusal is never a silent drop. main.ts: wired installBridges() into bootstrap — it was DEAD CODE (defined but never called), so window.* was undefined; the runtime slot probe needs it. GATES (R7 — codify, don't promise; shipped in the same patch). regimen_state_mutation_routing was RE-CODIFIED for the new N-ops→1-writer→1-key model: the old 1-fn↔1-key↔direct-set() model would have MISFIRED on the correct single-source design two ways (R9), the worst being that its body slice ran to the next `export function`, so the private writeSlotDoc got swallowed into whichever export preceded it — a placement-dependent false pass. NEW slot_invariants (static) proves the guard CODE exists (schema bounds, addSlot's cap-refusal, deleteSlot's last-refusal + activeSlot promotion); the runtime BEHAVIOUR is proven by the NEW render_probe_slots.js — the honest static/runtime split, because a Python-reads-TS gate cannot observe runtime state and selling static presence as runtime correctness is exactly the mineral-tiers failure. ## 2026-07-15 15:09 UTC-05:00 · incident · tools
design-system.css's seal was fingerprinted over this machine's CRLF bytes — a sequence git has never stored — so the critical gate was green only here and would RED on any fresh clone as if the sealed file were tampered with. Now LF-normalized like every other seal. Re-sealed.
  ↳ The design system's stylesheet is "sealed" — we store a fingerprint of it so that if anyone tampers with it, a check goes red. But the fingerprint had been taken of the file as it sits on THIS machine, with Windows line endings, while git stores the file with Unix line endings. So the fingerprint described a version of the file git has never stored. The check passed here and nowhere else: anyone cloning the repo fresh would get a CRITICAL red screaming that a sealed file had been tampered with, when nothing had. Fixed by fingerprinting the content in a line-ending-independent way — which is what every other sealed file in the project already did. This one was the only holdout. THE SHARPEST STATEMENT OF THE BUG: the golden recorded 37c338b7..., the sha256 of the 47,691-byte CRLF working tree. The committed blob is 46,563 bytes, LF, sha256 037d0e3e.... `git ls-files --eol` says `i/lf w/crlf`, and core.autocrlf=input does not convert on checkout. So the seal was anchored to bytes that exist on exactly one disk in the world. WHAT WAS FIXED - NEW _lf_file_hash() beside _file_hash() in tools/invariants.py — sha256 of LF-normalized content, matching corpus_seal/catalog_seal/products_seal's lf_sha256(). - check_design_system_hash_integrity switched to it (call site 558 ONLY). - _file_hash DELIBERATELY LEFT RAW. It has a live second caller at line 1968: the graphics gate. eden/graphics/*.jpg are marked `binary` in .gitattributes, git never EOL-converts them, and raw bytes ARE the truth there — LF-normalizing a JPEG's hash would corrupt that seal. Changing _file_hash globally was the obvious move and would have been wrong. - The golden re-sealed 37c338b7... -> 037d0e3e.... THE CSS CONTENT WAS NOT TOUCHED: `git diff --quiet design-system.css` is clean, and the new golden EQUALS the raw sha256 of the committed blob. The seal now anchors to bytes git actually stores. - .gitattributes: dashboard/assets/styles/*.css + *.golden.sha256 pinned `text eol=lf`. This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the fix — the gate is now EOL-agnostic regardless. It stops the working tree diverging from the blob again. - An EOL-aware hint added to the failure message: if the golden matches the file's RAW hash but not its LF hash, the message now says so explicitly ("a stale raw-byte seal, NOT a content edit"). A bare "hash mismatch" on a sealed canonical reads as tampering, and that misdiagnosis is expensive. - truth_anchor prose corrected. It said "raw-byte SHA-256" — accurate, and itself the defect being described. R9 — THE REFINEMENT SHIPS WITH ITS PROOF (tools/test_design_system_gates.py, 3 new cases) - eol_agnostic: the same content under LF and CRLF hashes identically AND equals the golden. This is the case the pre-fix gate fails. - content_edit_still_caught: THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the load-bearing half. A one-byte NON-EOL edit must STILL move the digest. Without it, "ignores line endings" could be satisfied by a function that ignores everything. A test that cannot reproduce the bug it guards proves nothing. - file_hash_still_raw: the raw hasher must still SEE an EOL difference, proving the split did not drift the binary graphics seal. - REPAIRED IN THE SAME PATCH: the pre-existing forged_hash_mismatch case patched inv._file_hash — which the fixed gate no longer calls. It would have gone GREEN against expect=RED. Repointed to _lf_file_hash. The audit predicted this exact failure before it happened. THE SWEEP (this was the point of auditing rather than spot-fixing): all 20 other goldens are already clone-stable, because their gates LF-normalize. Graphics raw-hashing is correct by construction. design-system was the sole holdout — so the fix adopts the existing pattern, it does not invent one. HONEST RED: invariants finished 68/69. design_system_write_protection is RED BY DESIGN — it anchors the working golden to `git show HEAD:<golden>` and reds while a golden is changed-but-uncommitted. That is the gate doing its job: it exists to catch an agent re-sealing SILENTLY, and a legitimate re-seal is supposed to be a visible, deliberate commit. It clears the moment this commit lands. Reported, not hidden, and not baselined. METHOD: found by a 37-agent adversarial audit (631 tool calls). Refuters killed several of the finders' own claims as materially overstated — including one that had the two hashes exactly backwards, and one that mis-named the gate the graphics concern applies to. Both were corrected before any code moved. The one thing that mattered most survived every attack: the committed blob is LF, and the golden was not.

TECHNICAL RECORD NEW INVARIANT `dose_amount_in_verbatim` (critical). Every claim's structured dose.amount must be literally present in that claim's OWN verbatim: unit-adjacent, scoped to the claim's own table row, and at the correct column index where dose.for_condition names one. Truth anchor: the claim's verbatim bytes, which corpus_integrity independently pins to the sealed book .txt. The three R2 gates now compose — R5/corpus_integrity proves the quote is the book's, this proves the number is the quote's, amounts_wallach_only proves the target is the number's. THE DESIGN WAS ATTACKED BEFORE IT SHIPPED, AND BROKEN THREE WAYS. All three are closed and pinned as tests: 1. CROSS-ROW BLEED. 72 of 86 claims accepted a fabrication drawn from their own verbatim, because 37 of 86 spans name more than one nutrient — the mined span routinely carries the NEXT table row. Closed by slicing the span on nutrient-NAME boundaries. 2. UNIT SWAP (the dangerous one). LETS-000048 choline 600 mg re-tagged `mcg` — a 1000x UNDER-dose — passed green, because chromium's row in the same span reads "300 to 600 mcg". This is the invisible failure mode: an understated target silently marks a user COVERED when they are not. LETS-000073 vitamin C mg -> IU passed off vitamin D's row (dimensionally nonsense, still certified). Critically, the spec's OWN proposed fix — "require the unit adjacent to the matched amount" — does NOT close this: 600 is adjacent to mg AND to mcg. Anyone implementing the documented remedy would have believed the axis closed while the live 1000x hole remained. Only row identity closes it. 3. IN-ROW COLUMN BLEED. The Let's Play Doctor base-line table prints NAME | RDA | true-supplement-need | pharmacologic, and dose.amount is column 1. So sodium 3,300 -> its own RDA 1,100 is a 3x understatement that presence-checking can never see. Closed by indexing the column positionally where for_condition declares it. Verified against real data: 30 rows column-checked, ZERO false-fires. WHAT SHAPED THE SCOPING. Row slicing keys on nutrient-name boundaries, NOT newlines, because table rows are sometimes space-joined on one line while prose is hard-wrapped mid-phrase. The discriminator is a follow-test: a name heads a table row iff a number (or a "?" placeholder) follows it, optionally past a form parenthetical ("Vitamin A (retinol) 2,500 IU"). In prose a name is followed by a word ("chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg"), which fails the test and leaves the span whole. This matters: an early newline-splitting design severed "Twenty to 30 mg ... for\ngermanium." from its own subject and RED-boarded a perfectly good claim. Every ambiguous path falls back to the FULL span — scoping may only ever tighten, never invent a narrower window that hides a mismatch. ZERO BASELINE EXCEPTIONS — and that is a finding, not a flourish. The original spec called for an R9 exception for the phosphorus-0 row ("PHOSPHORUS 800 mg 0.0 0.0"). An adversary proved that would have NEUTERED THE ENTIRE GATE: .claude/invariant-baseline.json is INVARIANT-scoped, not claim-scoped (stop_round_close.py::_tolerated returns a set of invariant NAMES), so a single entry would tolerate every fabrication across all 86 claims — and the spec's own mandated test would have been unsatisfiable. Handled in-gate instead: a unitless column is accepted ONLY when the amount is zero (0 mg == 0 mcg; Wallach's "0.0" means no supplemental need). A non-zero unitless column is unverifiable and fails closed. THE REAL DEFECT IT FOUND (1 of 86). WAL-CLM-RARE-000048 (selenium / Keshan disease) carried dose {amount: 1, unit: "mg", form: "sodium selenite"} but its verbatim span began AFTER the sentence containing that dose. The book source (eden/corpus/books/rare-earths-forbidden-cures.txt @430680) genuinely reads "...supplemented with 1 mg sodium selenite orally three times per week..." — so the dose was Wallach's and the SPAN was the defect. Fixed by widening the verbatim one sentence via eden/tools/vb_apply.py (mine_batch.py hard-rejects verbatim edits by design; verbatim changes are snap-owned). Before sealing I verified draft-vs-sealed across all 7 shards: exactly ONE claim differed, in exactly the two intended fields (verbatim, locator). Sealed at knowledge_version=333; embeds regenerated. Worth recording: this claim FALSE-PASSED a naive substring check, because "1" appears inside "1/1,000 children" — precisely the failure mode the gate exists to catch, and precisely why the digit-boundary lookarounds are load-bearing rather than cosmetic. THE TEST CAUGHT ME. tools/test_dose_amount_in_verbatim.py drives the impl with 20 planted, self-contained cases (mirroring real corpus shapes so they cannot rot on a re-seal) plus the real corpus. One case failed on first run — and the GATE was right, I was wrong: I had labeled "retinol -> 5,000 IU" as cross-row bleed, but 5,000 is retinol's OWN range top ("2,500 - 5,000 IU") AND target-equivalent under upper-of-range, so there was nothing to catch. Corrected to 25,000, which exists only in the beta-carotene row. The mislabeled case is kept in the file as a caution. FIXED EN ROUTE (all found by the same audit, all the same disease — confident prose over absent enforcement): - charter.md:29 called `no_operating_doc_contradiction` "future" when it is LIVE and critical. charter_gates_present cannot see it: its regex only parses R-table rows, and line 29 is prose. - charter.md R1 and data-flow.md:33 cited `eden_hash_integrity` + `eden_write_protection` as live invariants. NEITHER EXISTS. The former was deleted 2026-07-08 with the transitional eden-catalog.json it guarded (tombstone: invariants.py:357); the latter has no definition anywhere in the repo. I had also repeated `eden_hash_integrity` to Luneth in this session as a working gate — read out of a doc, restated as fact. Replaced with the real per-pillar seal gates (corpus_integrity, products_hash_integrity, catalog_integrity, graphics_integrity) plus the point that matters: a seal proves a pillar has not CHANGED, never that it is RIGHT. - CLAUDE.md:63/132/155 asserted every assets/data artifact is generated. The MANIFEST says 11 of 23 are hand_authored. The Charter was honest about this; CLAUDE.md — loaded every session as the operating contract — carried it unqualified. - CLAUDE.md §00.A and source-rule.md:16 named 6 books and omitted `hells-kitchen`, which is registered in books-meta AND carries 8 sealed claims. The §00.A allowlist did not cover a source already in use. The old shorthand tokens (`rbs`, `eps`) never matched the registry ids either. - 7 stale "EMPTY in H0/H1" comments claimed three live gates were vacuous; the tuples hold 4 and 2 real files and the gates bind. A comment that UNDERSELLS is not harmless — it invites a future reader to delete a working gate as dead weight. - pdm_coverage_derive.py's "33 trace_pdm" disambiguated. An auditor flagged it as drift against the canon's 35; it is NOT drift — the comment describes the runtime, and targets_derive overrides cobalt+tin to their own Wallach doses, so the shipped grouping really is 33. I did not "fix" a correct comment; I explained it, because the ambiguity fooled a careful reader. WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT CHECK (labeled, not hidden — R7): per_body_weight basis (13 of 14 spans carry no basis token; the "/100 pounds" header lives outside the quoted region); collective_group semantics (that DDDL-000115's 9 g is combined-not-each is asserted only in claim_text); period / form / duration / for_condition; column identity outside the one declared positional table; and whether a dose exists in the book but was never mined at all (that is mining_coverage_accounted's job). The 4 are hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen — forced to "covered" by a hardcoded list at state/coverage.ts:593 whose own comment cites "(Luneth)", not Wallach, because you breathe them. And "covered" turns out to mean four incommensurable things at once (measured from essentials-targets-data.json: wallach 38 · trace_pdm 33 sharing ONE PDM verdict amplified 33x · dietary_with_clinical_lever 14 · dietary 3 · unspecified 3; only 37 carry a numeric low>0). So "4/90" printed a count of four different kinds of thing as one fraction, twice, 200px apart. That is what "this box is honestly ugly" was reacting to — redundancy and incoherence are what ugly looks like before you can name it. The distribution replaces the ratio: COVERED 4 · PARTIAL 0 · PRESENT 0 · NOT COVERED 37 · NO WALLACH NUMBER YET 49, which needs no denominator and closes against the snapshot by construction. THE DECISION THAT REPLACED A BAD ONE. Claude argued — and tagged "Recommended" — that goals must leave Coverage PERMANENTLY because "Wallach says you need all 90 regardless, so a goal filter says some essentials matter less." Luneth accepted it, then reversed after thinking, and he was right: the corpus disproves it outright. The Catalog holds 512 conditions and 768 of 1,357 sealed claims (57%) map at least one; Let's Play Doctor IS a condition->protocol book. Most of what Wallach wrote is him answering "I have X, what do I take?" Luneth's read was the sharpest thing said all session: "my problem was never the idea, my problem was the presentation... 'What are you here for?' sounds rude, 'Let's get started' is more inviting. It was very simple all along and you blew it out of proportion." He flagged COPY; Claude escalated it into a doctrinal crisis about whether the concept may exist. That is the [[directives-are-guidelines-stay-balanced]] failure mode with a new face. THE RULE THAT RESOLVES IT (locked, now a memory). A goal may change what you LOOK AT, or what you're RECOMMENDED — never what you're MEASURED AGAINST. The denominator is always 90. The old goal cards' sin was never the goal, it was the DENOMINATOR: "bone & skeletal 3/14" asserts bone health IS 14 things, a subset, which inverts the thesis. Wallach's protocols are ADDITIVE — the 90 plus emphasis. And the honest version ARGUES FOR the 90: his answer to one condition is never narrow (arthritis 26 essentials across 4 of 4 categories, depression 24 across 4, cancer 18 across 4), so rendering his real answer makes the breadth case with zero copy. MEASURED, because the "$300/month to start" fear was load-bearing and false. Against the real product DB at wholesale, applying the real classify() thresholds: BTT 2.5 at $69.95 delivers 17 covered + 9 partial and, being the PDM vehicle, settles the whole 33-strong rare-earth group; reaching ~70/90 costs another $145 and 4 more products. The first $70 does more than the next $145 — and you can only SEE that if the denominator stays 90. A goal-filtered view hides the most motivating fact in the dataset. BUILT. coverage-A-plate / -B-band / -C-arrival, ALL SUPERSEDED BY coverage-D-personalized.html — the agreed vision. D: an unskippable blurred welcome taking a NAME + goals with "I'm just browsing" as the escape hatch (Luneth: "IF we can gather at least ONE piece of personal info RIGHT AWAY, THE REST OF THE APP IS SUDDENLY MUCH MORE POWERFUL"); a goal strip that REPORTS rather than asks, hover = transient focus, X revealed at 0px layout shift; goal membership on the tile EDGE while status keeps the interior — two channels, no collision — with MULTI-GOAL TILES WEARING A GRADIENT OF THEIR GOALS' HUES, emergent and true; the 33 rare earths as an always-required FOUNDATION third state rather than an absence; and a "Based on your goals" panel in the same gradient language using the EXISTING recommender score (.6/.3/.1, breadth saturating n/(n+5)), which un-flattened the list — Kid's Toddy ($26.95, 6.3/$10) outranks products supplying more for $48.95. The ledger stayed byte-identical before goals, after goals, and during hover. VERIFIED FOR LUNETH, who asked directly whether user data can ever poison Eden: it cannot, and it is an ABSENCE not a guard. eden/ is NEVER imported by the app (every mention in src/ is a comment); the pillars are read at BUILD time and baked into main.js; there is exactly ONE localStorage.setItem in the whole codebase (core/storage.ts:85). THE INSTRUMENT LIED THREE TIMES, twice producing a defect reported to Luneth as fact. (1) A ::after gradient ring rendered as nothing because .tile{overflow:hidden} clips the tile's OWN pseudo-element — invisible at 1x, obvious at 2x, and masked because single-goal rings looked perfect (box-shadow is NOT clipped by own-overflow). Fixed at the root — repeat(auto-fill, 92px) + gap:9px, chosen by measuring 8 combinations: integer tracks give integer positions and even rasterisation on all 4 sides, AND drop CHOLECALCIFEROL from 3 wrapped lines to 2, AND give lit neighbours air, AND wrap one tile earlier (13->12 cols) at only 5px slack. ## 2026-07-14 12:10 UTC-05:00 · incident · design-system
Reduced-motion block was strobing the app at ~100Hz for the users who asked for LESS motion — capped duration but never iteration-count; 7 painted offenders measured, fixed in one line, gated by a new render probe + proven with a negative test
  ↳ Anyone whose computer is set to "reduce motion" was getting a strobing page instead of a calm one — the exact opposite of what they asked for. The rule that was supposed to quiet our animations only capped how LONG each loop lasts, never how MANY times it repeats. So a 10-second loop told to take 0.01 seconds did not stop; it ran a hundred times per second. Seven things on screen were flashing. The fix is one line. The more important part is the new probe that makes it impossible to reintroduce — this bug was invisible to every gate we had, because the CSS said the right thing and did the opposite, so reading the code could never have caught it. Only measuring the real browser could. CAUSE. design-system.css:307-318, the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block, set `animation-duration: 0.01s !important` and `transition-duration: 0.01s !important` — and never set `animation-iteration-count`. Capping duration does not stop an `infinite` animation; it accelerates it 1000x. Measured headless (puppeteer, emulateMediaFeatures prefers-reduced-motion=reduce, verified honored by the browser): 7 PAINTED offenders at ~100Hz — ds-scan-sweep on .ds-scan-line (the worst: ramps opacity 0->0.35 while sweeping top from -3% to 103% across .essentials-host), ds-numeric-glow on .coverage-stat__num (the hero 13/90), ds-stat-pulse on .coverage-stat::before, ds-travel-top/-bottom on .coverage-hero::before/::after, and ds-pulse-animate on both .topbar__ask-dot and .topbar__workspace-tag::before. WCAG 2.3.1 puts the flash threshold at 3/sec. Honest severity: the scan-line is a real flash hazard (position + opacity over a large host); the other six are luminance shimmers on small or soft elements — genuinely wrong, not the same class. I am not going to inflate them. FIX. One declaration — `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` — inside the same block. design-system.css is SEALED; user sign-off is Luneth 2026-07-14 ("1. Yes"). Golden re-sealed cdf0ebd4... -> 37c338b7..., with the CSS written BEFORE the golden so design_system_write_protection's mtime rule (css_mtime > seal_mtime + 1 = violation) holds. Verified all 7 land on a benign 100% keyframe: off-screen (ds-travel-* at left/right 130%), opacity 0 (ds-scan-sweep at top 103%), or static (ds-numeric-glow 40px/0.4, ds-pulse-animate opacity 1, ds-stat-pulse opacity 0.32). Nothing is stranded mid-animation. R7 — THE GATE SHIPS IN THE SAME PATCH. New tools/render_probe_reduced_motion.js, anchored to the RENDERED computed style in a real browser under the real media feature (§00.B #11 — pin to a truth that cannot drift). Deliberately NOT a CSS-text grep: the source declared the right intent and did the opposite, which is precisely why no existing gate saw it, and a grep would be satisfied by a reworded rule or a comment. It generalises — any future animation added anywhere that loops fast under a reduce preference reddens this probe. PASS 2 is the anti-degenerate half: deleting every animation would trivially satisfy PASS 1, so the probe also asserts the ambient motion still runs for normal users. R9 — NEGATIVE TEST. A gate that has never gone red proves nothing. Reintroduced the bug via safe_write: probe FAILED, exit 1, all 7 offenders named at ~100Hz. Restored the fix: probe PASSED, exit 0. The CSS round-tripped byte-identical (sha256 == golden: True). A MEASUREMENT LESSON WORTH KEEPING. My first probe found only 5 offenders. getComputedStyle(el) with no pseudo argument never sees ::before/::after — and 4 of the 7 live entirely on pseudo-elements. A pseudo-blind animation scan undercounts by more than half. The shipped probe scans element + ::before + ::after. VERIFIED. build exit 0 · invariants 64/64, 0 new reds (design_system_hash_integrity + design_system_write_protection both green on the new seal) · render_probe.js exit 0 with the coverage DOM unchanged (tiles 60/16/12/3, covered 14, partial 12, gap 20, stat 13/90) · render_probe_reduced_motion.js exit 0 · normal-motion regression probe: all 7 ambient animations still at authored duration + infinite. On that last one — my regression probe reported a FAIL for ds-numeric-glow because I had hardcoded 3s as its expected duration; the CSS authors it at 4s (workspace-coverage.css:330). My expectation was wrong, not the code. Recording that rather than quietly correcting the constant. CONTEXT. Found while surveying Coverage for Luneth's over-arching UX notes (goals-first flow, top-bar overhaul, the living-light mesh). This is not a Coverage change and does not touch that work, which continues next.

  ↳ Plain: on a condition's page, the list of "nutrients to restore" used to sweep in nutrients that Wallach actually ties to a DIFFERENT disease — because some claims name many diseases and many minerals at once, and the old code just merged them all together. THE DEFECT (Audit B): the "nutrients to restore" (condition) and "works with" (essential) pills were computed by flattening essentials[] across MULTI-condition claims. A claim like WAL-CLM-RARE-000275 (a 10-condition x 10-mineral Rare-Earths deficiency list) handed osteoporosis all 10 minerals, so Zinc/Chromium/Selenium/Tin/Vanadium (which map to diabetes/immunity/cancer/deafness, never osteoporosis) leaked onto the page. Calcium -> {copper, magnesium, selenium, zinc} (its 3 real interaction claims), killing the "interacts with 41" inflation + the Gallium/Germanium/Tin/Oxygen phantoms. - co-occurrence stays ONLY for the violet "keep exploring" + related-conditions (serendipity), where broad is correct. PROMINENCE (item iii): corpus_embed.py now projects base_line_table (a claim tagged base-line-program / dose-table — a supplement-TABLE reference row, e.g. Fig. 8-1). entity_page_derive's protocol_claim_ids (the curated "what to do" source) EXCLUDES base-line-table dose rows, so a reference row never auto-fills a curated primary slot. ## 2026-07-11 09:05 UTC-05:00 · round-close · redesign
Redesign D3-P2 chunk 2: the Ask-Wallach ranking/synonym pass — lay terms now resolve (blood sugar→Diabetes, quicksilver→Mercury, b12→Cobalt), results are tier-scored, and homosexuality/intersex never surface in search unless explicitly named. Signed off.
  ↳ This is the second half of the "Ask Wallach" search: making it actually understand how people type. Before, you had to type the exact name; now the search knows Wallach's own everyday words for things — so "blood sugar" brings up Diabetes, "quicksilver" brings up Mercury, "b12" brings up Cobalt, "climate" brings up Carbon — and each result quietly notes which word matched ("via 'blood sugar'"). It also ranks results sensibly and, importantly, it will NOT show the homosexuality/intersex material unless someone explicitly searches those words — that content stays in the Explore index only. Luneth signed it off. Prototype-only — temporary/knowledge-drawer-prototype.html (gitignored demo; no pillar/artifact/app code touched, board stays 53/53). Data: re-injected CLAIMS carrying the full modern-voice `answer` text (real recall — fixes "sugar cravings", which lived in the answer body I'd dropped in chunk 1) + a resolved SEARCH_ENTITIES synonym table (the 56 search entities → {slug, name, k, syn}); all 56 resolve 1:1 to the browse ESS/CONDS/TOPICS (verified 0 misses), so synonyms attach to real pages. Logic: replaced the crude all-words searchClaims with a tiered-scoring suite. apTier scores a field exact(6) › prefix(5) › word-start(4) › substring(3). nameTier weights the display name ×20, an exact element symbol =100 (so "cr" → Chromium ranks with a name-prefix, tie broken by claim count), slug words ×12. aliasTier weights a synonym ×16 (between name and slug). rankEntities scans ESS/CONDS/TOPICS by name + the SEARCH_ENTITIES synonyms, dedups by k:slug taking the max score, and tags synonym-sourced rows with a "via <synonym>" hint. rankClaims scores each claim question(12)/subject(9)/answer_short(6)/answer(4) with per-query-word coverage(+2 each) and a +8 subject-boost when the query hit an entity's name/synonym (so "blood sugar" boosts every diabetes claim). Both replace the old searchAll/searchClaims calls in apRender. Charged-content gate (Luneth's explicit ask): CHARGED = {homosexuality, intersex}. chargedExplicit(q) marks a charged subject "explicitly named" only on a strong match — the entity name exact/prefix OR an EXACT synonym ("gay", "homosexual", "same-sex attraction", "lgbt"…), never an incidental substring. rankEntities filters charged entities out unless explicit; rankClaims skips charged-subject claims unless explicit. Result: "testosterone" and "sexual" no longer pull up homosexuality; "gay"/"homosexual"/"intersex" still do. The Explore tab is EXEMPT (it doesn't use these rankers) and remains the full categorised index. Testosterone/strength reality check: the corpus genuinely has no "increase testosterone / get stronger" content yet — the only "testosterone" hits are incidental mentions inside aromatherapy/cholesterol/homosexuality claims, and sexual_health has just 1 claim. So that's a MINING gap, not a code gap; I did not fake mappings (anti-fakery). Two follow-ups captured for the search-mining phase: (1) proactively mine + tag general-interest lay topics people search — men's-health / strength / vitality with lay synonyms ("increase testosterone", "get stronger", "build muscle", "stamina", "virility") — the ranking machinery is ready and will light up the moment the data is tagged, exactly like "blood sugar" does now; (2) the charged-search-gate becomes doctrine (port to the real search build) + backfill missing synonyms like "lesbian" → homosexuality. Verified headless: a ranking probe (blood sugar→Diabetes, quicksilver→Mercury, vitamin b12→Cobalt, cr→Chromium, sugar-cravings recall) + a gate probe (testosterone / how-to-increase-testosterone / sexual → NO homosexuality-or-intersex; gay / homosexual / intersex / same-sex attraction → shown), zero page errors, plus a screenshot of the "blood sugar → Diabetes (via 'blood sugar')" win. ## 2026-07-09 01:15 UTC-05:00 · round-close · tools
Phase-G task-zero: built the source-anchored substance triage buffer + its critical substance_triage_accounted gate — park an unmatched substance instead of typo-polluting the registry or dropping it. Board 52/52 (+1 gate); teeth proven by a 6-case negative test.
  ↳ We built the "honest escape hatch" for book mining, which resumes now that Phase G is unlocked. When the books mention a substance our nutrient registry doesn't know yet, it could be one of two things: an OCR typo off a noisy scanned page, or a genuinely-new herb Wallach names. The strict gate (references_resolve) already refuses to let a claim cite an unregistered substance. The danger was at the moment you fix that red board: the lazy move is to force the unmatched name — typo and all — into our pristine registry just to go green. This buffer is a third, legitimate exit: park the substance in a staging file with its source context and leave it out of the claim for now, so the board stays green honestly. Parking is now the LOWER-effort path than cheating, which is what drains the incentive to cheat. A separate accounting gate keeps the parked pile visible so it can't be silently forgotten — it turns RED if a book is ever marked fully-mined while it still has un-reviewed parked substances.
